title: A Zoology of Quantum Turing Patterns
abstract: We explore quantum Turing pattern zoology, where the same Lindblad equation supports a morphology atlas of stripes, spots, holes, labyrinths, and defects. The stable stripe species provides a quantitatively controlled case in which morphology and Gaussian witness loss separate parametrically. In particular, visible Turing stripes can remain after two Gaussian witness margins associated with the same $k_*$ mode cross zero in a completely positive Lindblad lattice. The witness thresholds on the exact shell fall as $\mathcal{N}^{-1}$. The stripe nematic threshold tends to a nonzero value at fixed lattice size, time window, and morphology criterion. The ratio of the morphology threshold to either witness threshold therefore grows with $\mathcal{N}$. Imaging and momentum-resolved covariance measurements probe these sectors separately.
summary: This work explores the rich 'zoology' of quantum Turing patterns supported by a single Lindblad equation. It rigorously demonstrates that macroscopic morphological order (like stripes) can persist even when standard measures of quantum entanglement (Gaussian witnesses) suggest their absence. The findings highlight a quantitative separation between these two distinct types of order as the system size increases.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum Turing pattern zoology, exploring how a single Lindblad equation can support a diverse morphology atlas (stripes, spots, holes, etc.). It specifically focuses on the separation between macroscopic order and quantum correlations.
main_result: Visible Turing stripes can persist even when Gaussian entanglement witnesses cross zero, and the threshold for morphology order grows parametrically with system size ($N$) relative to the witness thresholds.
method: The analysis uses the Lindblad master equation to model system dynamics, calculating mean values and fluctuations via the covariance matrix evolution. Key diagnostics include Gaussian witnesses and morphology measures.
model_or_system: The system is a periodic array of bosonic modes governed by a Lindblad equation involving a Hamiltonian and jump operators, describing parametrically driven nonlinear resonators.
key_observables: Stripe nematicity, Gaussian witnesses (NPT, P-witness), covariance matrix asymmetry (USB), and various morphology thresholds ($\Theta_c^M$).
important_parameters: System size ($N$), lattice size ($L$), and various coupling/gain/loss parameters defining the Lindblad generator.
main_assumptions: The analysis compares finite-$N$ results to the $N 	o \infty$ limit and relies on linearizing the fluctuation dynamics around mean values.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the morphology atlas (Fig. 1), momentum space structure and witness crossings (Fig. 2), and the parametric separation of morphology and witness thresholds (Fig. 4).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the dynamics using the Lindblad equation, first characterizing the full morphology space, then quantifying quantum correlations using witnesses, and finally demonstrating the parametric separation between these two types of order.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical framework for distinguishing between different types of order (classical/morphological vs. quantum/entanglement) in open quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding pattern formation in quantum optics and condensed matter.
